summary: Tested 'Cerca utente' (GET /api/datto/user-search + topbar UserSearch) and 'Collega MAC virtuali' (datto_mac_links in device-info, datto_users_for, user-search). 8 of 10 backend tests passed. The frontend flow worked end to end on desktop and mobile: search, results, empty state, clear button, and clicking a location opened the switch page with port 7 selected and the Vista Cavo modal showing. Two backend bugs: results include devices of clients that no longer exist, and locating a PC by MAC fails when the scanner stored the MAC in lowercase or without separators.

critical.issue: Results are not limited to clients that exist. The datto_devices query has no check against db.clients. In preview, 12 results came from the deleted clients ae6eb96b/1c04e486/588ea729 (27PADELSRV, SRVDC, SRVDATI, win11tv, each listed 3 times). client_name falls back to the raw UUID, and the dropdown shows it. Fix: load the existing client ids first, then add {client_id: {$in: ids}} to the datto_devices query.

minor.issue: The MAC match is an exact string compare against discovered_endpoints.mac. Datto/link MACs are uppercase with colons, but scanner endpoints are often lowercase ('9c:75:14:50:c1:45') or bare ('aaaa00000001'): 14 of 20 endpoints in preview are lowercase. An endpoint with mac '00:15:5d:01:79:0d' and a non-matching IP was not located. Fix: query with all format variants (upper, lower, bare) or a case-insensitive regex. Currently only the IP fallback hides the problem.
Same exact-match risk if callers pass MACs that are not normalized. Make sure callers pass _norm_mac()'d MACs.

integration_issues.issue: Orphan-client results show the client UUID instead of a name (caused by the backend issue above)

issues: Responses that arrive out of order are not discarded or cancelled, so a slow reply to an earlier query can overwrite the results of a later one (minor).
While a new query loads, the old results stay on screen with no spinner, because loading && !res is false when res already exists.

action_items: user_search.py: keep only devices whose client_id exists in db.clients
user_search.py _locate: match endpoint MACs regardless of case and separators (upper, lower, bare 12-hex)
Optional: UserSearch.jsx: ignore out-of-order responses and show a loading state when the query changes
critical_code_review_comments: _backfill_last_user runs on every search request. It is cheap once all devices have last_user, but it still issues a query each time. Consider running it at Datto sync time instead.
_locate runs up to 3 queries per result (up to 50 results), an N+1 pattern. It is acceptable at the current scale.
device-info: remember_mac_link uses d.client_id, while _linked_device filters on the client_id passed in the request. These are consistent, because IP and name lookups use allow_global=False.
seed_data_creation: Temporary data only, all removed: TEST_sw_iter166 managed switch at 10.10.1.2, a TEST_iter166 discovered_endpoint (port 7), a TEST_iter166 port_memory row, and a TEST_iter166fe endpoint on 10.10.41.220 port 7 used for the UI deep link. datto_mac_links is back to 0 documents. Side effect: the backfill test unset last_user on SRVDATI86B, and the backfill restored it to 'SRVDATI86B\Administrator'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin token is cached in /tmp/argus_tok. For UI tests, inject it with localStorage 'noc_token' so you do not need to log in again. CHASW-B at 10.10.41.220 (client da3d6e40) has 26 ports and is the right target for deep links. After the fixes, rerun test_user_search_only_existing_clients and test_user_search_location_lowercase_mac.
rca of the issue: Orphan results: user_search queries datto_devices by last_user only. Devices from Datto sites whose clients were deleted are still in datto_devices, so they show up. Lowercase MAC: _locate uses $in with exact-case Datto MACs, but discovered_endpoints stores the scanner's raw MAC format.
